newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says euro debate unsettling markets.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says euro debate unsettling markets.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Friday a delay in the launch of Europe's planned single currency, the euro, would cause turbulence on currency markets, as well as German growth and exports losses.

Waigel, addressing a meeting of the district branch of his Christian Social Union (CSU) party in Nuremberg, said a political debate in Germany over whether the euro should be delayed or not was unsettling for currency markets.

Waigel said a delay in European economic and monetary union (EMU) would lead to "turbulence on currency markets and then very quickly to export losses" for Germany and this would also mean economic growth would slow down.
"Of course we must expect the others (countries wanting to join EMU) to adhere to the criteria, but the others are entitled to expect us to be trustworthy," Waigel told fellow CSU party colleagues.

He called on his party, the more conservative sister of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats, which only exists in Bavaria, to be more open towards EMU. Many senior figures in the CSU have called for a delay in EMU if France or other countries fail to meet the economic criteria to join.
But he urged them to look at Britain, where the Conservative party lost the last general election in May "because it was not open" in its European policy.
